journal_lines: The woodcutter cleared the slope. The miner found what was underneath. Neither would have managed alone.
Roots had grown into the seam. Cut through to reach it. Took both of them.
Timber over ore. Cleared the one to reach the other. Long day, good result.
The outcrop needed clearing. The clearing became lumber. The lumber revealed stone.
Timber fell across the cave mouth. Removed the timber. Found the cave useful.
Two disciplines sharing a hillside. Both productive.
Woodcutting opened the slope. Mining finished the day.
The roots had grown into the seam. First the roots, then the ore.
Cut through the forest floor to reach the stone below. Worth both efforts.
The tree was in the way of the mine. The mine was under the tree. Both resolved.
Surface work and deep work in one place. Rare and efficient.
The forest above fed the mine below. Removed both in the right order.
